extracted.subtask_description: Review the lesson website (homepage, all episode pages, and Extras such as Setup and Instructor Notes) for readiness to teach in The Carpentries Lab, focusing on accessibility, content accuracy, pedagogy, and supporting materials. Post the review in the lesson's GitHub issue thread and follow the repository communication/process rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative text for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The alternative text of all figures is accurate and sufficiently detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large or complex figures may not be fully described in the image alt text and instead should be described elsewhere in the episode body. To check alt text, use accessibility tools (e.g. WAVE), inspect the HTML image element, or consult the source (R)Markdown file. See provided links 'How to Design Great Alt Text: An Introduction' and 'Writing Alt Text for Data Visualization' for more guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid colloquialisms and region/culture-specific references
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson content does not make extensive use of colloquialisms, region- or culture-specific references, or idioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer language that is broadly accessible to an international audience and learners from diverse backgrounds; flag phrases that may be confusing or culturally specific and suggest neutral alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid contractions
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson content does not make extensive use of contractions (e.g. “can’t” vs “cannot”, “we’ve” vs “we have”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more formal wording to improve clarity and accessibility, especially for learners for whom English is a second language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to The Carpentries Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson content conforms to The Carpentries Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must be familiar with the Code of Conduct and flag any content or tone that conflicts with it. By accepting the invitation to review, reviewers agree to abide by the Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meets the authors' stated objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson meets the objectives defined by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that lesson- and episode-level objectives are present and that content, exercises, and assessments align with and support those objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate for the identified target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson is appropriate for the target audience identified for the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that assumed prior knowledge, pacing, examples, and difficulty match the stated audience. If mismatch, recommend revising audience statement or content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson content is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check factual correctness of explanations, code, commands, outputs, and any domain claims; point out errors or ambiguous statements and provide corrections or references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive and easy to understand
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson is descriptive and easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review readability: clear explanations, well-chosen examples, minimal jargon or when used it is defined; suggest rewordings or restructuring where prose is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure manages cognitive load
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson is appropriately structured to manage cognitive load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check sequencing of topics, chunking of material, use of incremental examples, and whether learners are overloaded with simultaneous new concepts/tools. Recommend reorganizing or simplifying where cognitive load is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: No dismissive language
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson does not use dismissive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag wording that belittles learners' experiences, assumes shortcuts, or dismisses alternative approaches; suggest inclusive and respectful phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool choice is open-source or justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools used in the lesson are open source or, where tools used are closed source/proprietary, there is a good reason for this (e.g. no open source alternatives are available or widely-used in the lesson domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proprietary tools are used, ensure the authors document rationale and accessibility implications; suggest open alternatives where practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example data sets accessibility and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any example data sets used in the lesson are accessible, well-described, available under a CC0 license, and representative of data typically encountered in the domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm dataset availability, metadata/description quality, and appropriate licensing (CC0). If datasets are missing, proprietary, or poorly described, request improvements or replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superfluous data sets
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson does not make use of superfluous data sets (e.g. increasing cognitive load by introducing a new data set instead of reusing another present in the lesson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend reusing existing datasets in the lesson when possible to reduce unnecessary complexity and focus learners on target skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example tasks and narrative are appropriate and realistic
rubrics_metrics.description: The example tasks and narrative of the lesson are appropriate and realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether examples reflect genuine domain problems and realistic workflows; suggest more realistic or domain-relevant scenarios if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise solutions are accurate and explained
rubrics_metrics.description: The solutions to all exercises are accurate and sufficiently explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check provided solutions for correctness and pedagogical value; recommend expanding terse solutions with explanatory steps or rationale where students need guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion exercises have instructor guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any discussion exercises without solutions are accompanied by sufficient information/guidance so that Instructors can judge whether the discussion's learning objectives have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure instructor notes include expected talking points, assessment criteria, or example outcomes for discussion prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of exercise formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The lesson includes exercises in a variety of formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a mix of short-answer, coding, multiple-step problems, formative checks, and discussion prompts to support varied assessment and engagement strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise difficulty appropriate for expected experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise tasks and formats are appropriate for the expected experience level of the target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure exercises neither overwhelm novices nor bore experienced learners; recommend adjustments in complexity or scaffolding as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives are assessed (formative assessment present)
rubrics_metrics.description: All lesson and episode objectives are assessed by exercises or another opportunity for formative assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm every stated objective has at least one corresponding assessment or practice opportunity; suggest adding formative checks where objectives lack assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises have diagnostic power
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises are designed with diagnostic power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer exercises that reveal specific misunderstandings or skill gaps (not just 'do this'); recommend redesigning tasks to diagnose competency where current exercises are purely procedural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning objectives are clear, descriptive, measurable, and skill-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning objectives for the lesson and its episodes are clear, descriptive, and measurable. They focus on the skills being taught and not the functions/tools (e.g. “filter the rows of a data frame based on the contents of one or more columns,” rather than “use the filter function on a data frame”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit objectives to be action-oriented and assessable; avoid objectives framed only as using a particular tool or function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience statement specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The target audience identified for the lesson is specific and realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete descriptors (prior experience, domain, expected skill level) rather than vague audiences; request clarification if too broad or unrealistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of required prior skills/knowledge is complete and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of required prior skills and/or knowledge is complete and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify prerequisite lists match actual content demands and recommend adding or removing items to accurately reflect what learners must know beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup and installation instructions are complete and usable
rubrics_metrics.description: The setup and installation instructions are complete, accurate, and easy to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test or carefully read setup steps for missing commands, platform-specific issues, or unclear steps; request clearer instructions, troubleshooting tips, or automated environment files if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary completeness or external links
rubrics_metrics.description: No key terms are missing from the lesson glossary or are not linked to definitions in an external glossary (e.g. Glosario).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for essential terminology used without definition and recommend adding glossary entries or linking to authoritative external glossaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review: lesson website only
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of your review is limited to the contents of the lesson website; you do not need to review other files in the lesson repository that do not form part of the lesson site itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewers find issues in repository files not present on the site, they should contact the Editor who invited them rather than treating those files as part of the standard site review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read all lesson pages and Extras
rubrics_metrics.description: When making your review, read through the lesson homepage and all the episode pages, as well as the pages under the Extras dropdown (Setup, Instructor Notes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness by checking homepage, each episode, and Extras material so reviewer comments consider the full learner and instructor experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide general comments on readability, coverage, comparisons, and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should make general comments about the readability of the lesson; any key concepts or skills missing; how it compares to other learning resources; and its utility for Instructors and self-directed learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-level feedback on strengths/weaknesses, missing topics, and practical usefulness in addition to line-item checklist comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use single GitHub issue thread for review communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole review process for a lesson is intended to take place in a single issue thread, with Reviewers posting their reviews and comments as replies to the original submission and authors posting responses in the same thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep review and author responses consolidated in the issue thread to maintain a single public record of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report issues/PRs and link them in your review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are allowed — encouraged — to open issues and pull requests to report and address areas for improvement; if you do this, include links to these contributions in your review report when you post it to the thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you fix content via a PR or note problems via issues, explicitly reference those links in the review to connect proposed/implemented changes with the review discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize external communications in the thread
rubrics_metrics.description: If you communicate with the authors about the lesson and review outside of the issue thread, summarise, link to, and/or quote these conversations within the thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves transparency and keeps the public review record complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct agreement on acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting the invitation to review a lesson, you are agreeing to abide by The Carpentries Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure they understand the Code and behave accordingly during the review process (tone, respect, confidentiality expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Reviewer Checklist template
rubrics_metrics.description: This checklist is available as a template for you to use when preparing your review to post to the issue thread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a copy of the Reviewer Checklist to guide your review, but reviewers may also comment beyond the listed points and provide broader feedback.
